_readme: MACHINE-OWNED. Appended to by the scheduled Soundings run; do not hand-edit except to
DELETE an entry you would rather not have published. Deleting is always safe — nothing
reads back what it wrote, so a removed entry never returns.
This is the THIRD file, and the reason it is a third file rather than a key in content.json
is the same reason feeds.json exists: content.json is Brenden's, and an automated writer
must have no way to clobber his words. Two owners, two files, no overlap.
The rules the writer follows are in SOUNDINGS.md. Read that before adding anything.

entries.text: Blue whale songs have been getting deeper for decades. Recordings going back to the sixties show the pitch dropping year after year, in every population around the world at once, and nobody's got a good explanation for it.

The kelp was a column of glyphs and didn't read as kelp at all. The character was fine — the spacing wasn't. One every ninety units meant 94% of each stalk was open water, and no glyph closes a gap that size. It needed a continuous shape.

Every whale shark has its own pattern of spots behind the gills, so you can tell individuals apart from photos. The software researchers use to match them came out of astronomy — it was built to line up star fields.

The clouds in the world looked blocky, because they were the same shade glyphs as the haze stamped along a sine wave. The title screen already had proper wispy ones, so the world calls the title's painter now. One wisp in the codebase instead of two that drift apart.

A humpback's flippers are about a third of its body — five metres, the longest arm on any animal. The front edge is lumpy instead of smooth, and those bumps are what let something that size make tight turns underwater.

Menus use spatial navigation: press right and focus goes to whatever's physically to the right. Turned up a good bug — maxed upgrade cards were marked disabled, which pulled them out of the focus list, so the card you'd finished was the one you couldn't select or refund.

Fin whales are painted differently on each side. The right of the lower jaw is white and the left is dark grey. Nobody's sure why, but they tend to roll onto their right side when they feed, so the white ends up facing down at the fish.

The circular rainbow rails were coming out solid black. A gradient runs from the rail's first point to its last, and a loop ends where it starts — so both ends are one point, and a gradient across no distance paints nothing. Closed rails get a conic gradient instead.

Belugas can turn their heads. Nearly every other whale has its neck bones fused into one solid block, so head and body move as one piece. A beluga's aren't fused, so it can nod and look sideways at you.

Controller support means polling: the browser never tells you a stick moved, so you ask it every frame, forever. The harder problem is knowing what someone's actually holding — pick up a pad and the mouse pointer clears off, then comes back when you touch the mouse.

Humpbacks catch fish by blowing a ring of bubbles around them. One whale swims a spiral underneath, the wall of bubbles herds the fish into a tight ball, and the whole group comes up through the middle with their mouths open.

A big splash throws up more droplets than the game can afford, so there's a hard cap on live particles. I was worried it was deleting ones you'd actually see, and when I sat still and tested it, it was. Flying properly you've already left them behind.

Baleen whales don't shed earwax — it builds up in layers over their whole lives, like tree rings. Count the layers and you've got the whale's age, and there's enough hormone left in each one to tell when it was stressed or breeding.

The clouds and the big rock arch slid past at the same rate as everything near you, so the backdrop read flat. Put them on parallax, and the same number that sets how slowly a thing drifts also sets how much it fades — so nothing can look distant and move like it's close.

When a whale dies its body sinks, and it feeds a whole community on the seafloor for decades. There are worms down there with no mouth and no gut that grow roots into the bones and live off the fat inside. Nobody knew they existed until about twenty years ago.

Drawing the night sky one star at a time was the most expensive thing in the game, so I cached it — paint the sky once, reuse the picture. That kills the twinkle though, since every star's stuck on the same instant. So 6% stay live and the rest sit at their average.

A narwhal's tusk is really a tooth — the left canine, grown straight out through the lip, and it's packed with nerve endings. Drones caught them a few years ago using it to tap fish and stun them, which nobody had managed to film before.

The whale shark's got way more detail on it than anything else in the game, and when it's swimming fast it leaves a trail of fading copies of itself behind. All that was enough to drop the game to half speed any time it was on screen.
Every whale skin up to now has been one flat colour. There is a patterned one now, a green camo, and it looks better in the water than I expected.
Someone managed to get a heart monitor onto a wild blue whale a few years ago. On a deep dive its heart slowed to two beats a minute, then climbed back up once it surfaced to breathe.

Killer whales are one of the very few animals that go through menopause. Females live for decades after their last calf, and when the salmon are thin the pod follows the oldest one around, because she is the one who remembers where the fish turn up.
Been filming the game rather than playing it this week. A camera parked in one spot notices things a camera chasing a whale never has to.

Cuvier's beaked whales hold the record for staying under. One tagged off North Carolina managed a single breath-hold of three hours and forty-two minutes, and the species has been logged just shy of three kilometres down.
Some of the new paint jobs came out so dark the whale stopped having an outline — just a whale-shaped hole moving through the water. Very striking, and sent straight back to wardrobe.

Bowhead whales keep turning up with 19th-century harpoon points still lodged under the blubber, healed over and filed away. Racemization in the eye lens puts the oldest of them somewhere past two hundred years, which means a few of them were already swimming when the harpoons were new.
The whale used to bend in exactly one place, like a door. It bends along its whole length now, and it is insufferable about it.

Humpback song travels like a hit single. A new tune starts off eastern Australia and works its way east across the South Pacific, population by population, until everyone out by French Polynesia is singing this year's version and nobody is doing last year's.
The whale had been quietly drawing itself a fraction of a second in the past. Extremely on-brand behaviour for a whale, and it has now been asked to join the rest of us in the present.
Sperm whales sleep standing up. Whole pods of them go vertical, nose to the surface, and drift there like a filing cabinet nobody wants to open.
A number on the screen would not stop showing off, even after being switched off. It has been sat down. There is no story here and we will not be taking questions.
Baleen is not bone. It is keratin — the same stuff as your fingernails — which means the largest animals that have ever lived are straining dinner through a moustache.
The ocean costs less to draw than it did last week. It looks exactly the same. That is the whole achievement and I would like it noted.
